Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 25 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Cabinet Approves Two Mega Hydro Power Projects Worth Rs.40,175.33 Crore in AR In April 2026, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, has approved two mega hydroelectric projects in Arunachal Pradesh (AR) with a combined investment of Rs. 40,175.33 crore to boost renewable energy, strengthen energy security, and promote sustainable development in the North-Eastern region. • The projects comprise the 1200 megawatt (MW) Kalai-II Hydro Electric Project (HEP) in Anjaw District and the 1720 MW Kamala HEP across Kamle, Kra Daadi, and Kurung Kumey Districts. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Approved 2 Mega Hydro Power Projects at Rs.40,175.33 Crore in AR ✓ Nodal Authority: Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) ✓ Projects: ✓ Kalai-II Capacity: 1200 MW (Lohit River) at Rs.14,105.83 crore. ✓ Kamala Capacity: 1720 MW (Kamle/Kra Daadi/Kurung Kumey) at Rs.26,069.50 crore. ✓ Implementation Partners: THDC India Limited (Kalai-II) and NHPC Limited (Kamala). About Kalai-II Hydro Electric Project: Project: The CCEA approved Rs.14,105.83 crore for the Kalai-II Hydro Electric Project (HEP) on the Lohit River in Anjaw District, AR, which includes development of around 29 kilometres (km) of roads and bridges to improve local connectivity in Namsai and Anjaw Districts. Capacity: The Kalai-II HEP has an installed capacity of 1,200 MW (6 × 190 MW + 1 × 60 MW), is expected to generate 4,852.95 Million Units (MU) annually, and is planned for completion within 78 months. Implementation: The project will be executed through a Joint Venture (JV) between THDC India Limited (formerly Tehri Hydro Development Corporation) and the Government of AR. Financial Support: The Government of India (GoI) will provide Rs.599.88 crore for enabling infrastructure, including roads, bridges, and transmission lines, and Rs.750 crore as Central Financial Assistance (CFA) toward the State’s equity share. Benefits: The State will receive 12% free power and an additional 1% for the Local Area Development Fund (LADF), while the project will support peak demand management, national grid balancing, infrastructure development, employment, compensation, and CSR initiatives. Significance: Kalai-II HEP is the first hydroelectric project in the Lohit Basin, strengthening power supply and socio-economic growth in the region. About Kamala Hydro Electric Project: Investment: The CCEA approved Rs.26,069.50 crore for the Kamala HEP in Kamle, Kra Daadi, and Kurung Kumey Districts, AR, including Rs.4,743.98 crore for flood moderation, Rs.1,340 crore for enabling infrastructure, and Rs.750 crore as Central Financial Assistance (CFA) for the State’s equity share. Capacity: The project has an installed capacity of 1,720 MW (8 × 210 MW + 1 × 40 MW) and is expected to generate 6,870 MU annually, supporting peak demand management, national grid balancing, and flood moderation in the Brahmaputra valley. Implementation: Kamala HEP will be executed through a JV between NHPC Limited (National Hydroelectric Power Corporation) and the Government of AR, with an estimated completion period of 96 months. Infrastructure: Around 196 km of roads and bridges, along with essential facilities such as hospitals, schools, and marketplaces

About Arunachal Pradesh (AR): Chief Minister (CM) – Pema Khandu Governor – Lieutenant (Lt) General Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik (Retired) Capital – Itanagar National Park (NP) – Mouling NP, Namdapha NP Cabinet Approves NBS Rates for Kharif 2026, Jaipur Metro Phase-II, and HRRL Refinery Expansion In April 2026, the Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, approved a series of significant proposals aimed to strengthen India’s agricultural support systems, enhance urban infrastructure, and boost energy security. These approvals include: • Rs 41, 534 crore Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for the Kharif Season 2026 on Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) fertilisers; • The development of the Jaipur Metro Phase-II project in Rajasthan, estimated cost Rs 13,037.66 crore; and • The revision in cost and equity investment for the HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Limited (HRRL) at Pachpadra in Rajasthan. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Cabinet Approvals on April 8, 2026 ✓ Approval-1: NBS rates for Kharif Season, 2026 on P&K Fertilizers ✓ Budget: Rs.41,533.81 crore ✓ Implementation Dates: From April 01, 2026 to September 30, 2026 ✓ Purpose: To ensure smooth availability of NPKS fertilizers to farmers at affordable rates ✓ Approval-2: Jaipur Metro Phase-2 Project ✓ Budget: Rs 13,037.66 crore ✓ Implementing Agency: RMRCL (50:50 JV between GoI and the Government of Rajasthan) ✓ Connects: Prahladpura to Todi Mod (in Rajasthan) ✓ Approval-3: Revision in cost and equity investment for HRRL ✓ Location of Project: Pachpadra in Rajasthan ✓ Revised Cost: Rs.79,459 crore (up from Rs. 43,129 Crore) ✓ Implementing Agency: HRRL, a JV of HPCL (74%) and GoR (26%) NBS rates for Kharif Season, 2026 on P&K fertilizers The Union Cabinet approved the proposal of the Department of Fertilizers (DoF) which works under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (MoC&F), for fixing the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for Kharif Season, 2026, starting from April 01, 2026 to September 30, 2026, on P&K fertilizers, with tentative budgetary allocation of Rs.41,533.81 crore.

# Page 27^page=27
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 27 Daily Content PDF • The budgetary allocation for Kharif season 2026 marks an increase of nearly 12% compared to Rs. 37,216.15 crore for Kharif 2025 season. Key Details: Benefits: Availability of fertilizers to farmers at subsidized, affordable and reasonable prices will be ensured. Implementation: The subsidy on P&K fertilizers which include Diammonium Phosphate (DAP) and NPKS grades (which indicates the percentage by weight of Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K) and Sulphur (S)) will be provided based on approved rates for Kharif 2026, ensuring smooth availability of these fertilizers to the farmers at affordable prices. About NBS: The subsidy on P&K fertilizers is administered by the NBS Scheme, Central Sector Scheme (CSS), launched by DoF on April 01, 2010. • Aim: To provide government support for P&K (Phosphatic and Potassic) fertilizers based on nutrient content: N, P, K, and S rather than the product, ensuring affordability, balanced soil nutrition, and enhanced productivity for farmers. • Subsidy Disbursement Process: Subsidies are paid to manufacturers/importers, which are passed on to farmers through reduced Maximum Retail Prices (MRP), while subsidies on urea are managed separately. • NPKS Grades: At present, the Government of India (GoI) makes available 28 grades of P&K fertilizers including DAP to farmers at subsidized rates through fertilizer manufacturers/importers. Cabinet Approves Jaipur Metro Project Phase-2: The Union Cabinet has also approved Jaipur Metro Phase-2, a transformative 41 km North–South corridor from Prahladpura to Todi Mod comprising 36 stations, with an estimated cost Rs 13,037.66 crore. • The approved metro project is expected to be completed by September 2031. Key Details: Implemented by: The project will be implemented by Rajasthan Metro Rail Corporation Limited (RMRCL), a 50:50 Joint Venture (JV) of the Government of India and the Government of Rajasthan (GoR). Boost Connectivity: This newly approved corridor will provide seamless connectivity to major activity nodes in Rajasthan such as Sitapura Industrial Area, Vishwakarma Industrial Area (VKIA), Jaipur Airport, Tonk Road, SMS Hospital and Stadium, Ambabari and Vidhyadhar Nagar. Funding: The project is funded through the equity support from the GoI and Government of Rajasthan, subordinate debt and multilateral financing, aligns with the Metro Rail Policy, 2017. Significance: It is expected to significantly reduce traffic congestion, lower vehicular emissions and enhance mobility for residents, workers and tourists. Phase-I: At present, the metro system under Phase-1, running along the East–West corridor from Mansarovar to Badi Chaupar, including 11.64 km with 11 stations which connects important residential & commercial areas with the Central Business District of Jaipur, is operational in the state. Cabinet Approves Revised Cost for HRRL in Rajasthan: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the PM Narendra Modi has approved the revised cost of HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Limited (HRRL) project cost from Rs. 43,129 Crore to Rs.79,459 Crore. • In addition, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) will invest additional equity investment of Rs.8,962 crore, following this, the total equity investment by HPCL reaches to Rs.19,600 crore. Key Details: HRRL: HRRL, located at Pachpadra, Balotra district in Rajasthan, is a 9 Million Metric Tonnes Per Annum (MMTPA) greenfield Refinery-cum- Petrochemical Complex with 2.4 MMTPA petrochemical production

# Page 28^page=28
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 28 Daily Content PDF capacity. Implemented by: The Project is being implemented by HRRL, a Joint Venture (JV) of HPCL and Government of Rajasthan (GoR) with equity stakes of 74% and 26% respectively. Significance: HRRL refinery is expected to produce 1 MMTPA of Polypropylene, 0.5 MMTPA of LLPDE (Linear Low Density Polyethylene), 0.5 MMTPA of HDPE (High Density Polyethylene) and about 0.4 MMTPA of Benzene, Toluene and Butadiene, which are critical for energy and industrial ecosystem in sectors like transportation, pharma, paints, packaging industries etc. Operationalisation: The refinery is scheduled to fully operationalise on 1st July, 2026. About Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL): Chairman & Managing Director (CMD) – Vikas Kaushal Headquarters – Mumbai, Maharashtra Established – 1974 Union Minister Jayant Chaudhary Initiates Campaign to Build ‘Skills Outcomes Fund’ for Youth Livelihoods In April 2026, Union Minister of State (MoS) (Independent Charge, IC) Jayant Chaudhary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), initiated a campaign to establish the Skills Outcomes Fund (SOF), a first-of-its-kind initiative, in New Delhi, Delhi, to enhance employment opportunities for youth from low-income backgrounds across India. • The initiative aims to launch the SOF to mobilize capital, link skilling to verified employment outcomes for youth, and scale as the world’s largest Outcomes-Based Financing (OBF) initiative. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Skills Outcomes Fund (SOF) campaign launched ✓ By Whom? Union MoS (IC) Jayant Chaudhary, MSDE ✓ Nodal Agency: NSDC ✓ Model: Outcomes-Based Financing (OBF) ✓ Objective: Unlock aspirational livelihoods for low-income youth via OBF ✓ Precursor: Skill Impact Bond ✓ Key Focus: Employment outcomes (placement, retention). ✓ Target sectors: IT-ITeS, BFSI, automotive, healthcare, logistics, green jobs, electronics. About SOF and OBF: SOF: It is a financing mechanism that links funding to measurable employment outcomes such as job placement, retention, and career progression, shifting focus from enrolment and certification to jobs and income. OBF: It links investments to measurable, verified employment outcomes, shifting the focus from enrolment and certification to job placement, retention, and career progression. Key Features of SOF: Anchor: Led by National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) under the MSDE as the nodal implementing agency. Model: Uses blended finance by combining government, private, and philanthropic capital through an outcomes-based financing approach linking payments to verified employment results. Focus: Targets demand-driven, employer-led skilling in high-growth sectors such as Information Technology – Information Technology Enabled Services (IT-ITeS), Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI), healthcare, logistics, green jobs, and electronics. Verification: Ensures payments only after independent validation of job placement, retention, and career progression outcomes.

# Page 29^page=29
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 29 Daily Content PDF Ecosystem: Involves public sector (Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL), Hindustan Urvarak & Rasayan Limited (HURL)), philanthropy (Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Michael & Susan Dell Foundation, Children’s Investment Fund Foundation), and corporates (JSW Foundation, Bajaj Finserv, JPMorgan, NSE Foundation, Hindustan Unilever). Alignment: Supports Viksit Bharat 2047 by advancing accountable, outcome-oriented skilling aligned with the draft National Policy for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (NPSDE) 2026, to drive efficient and sustainable livelihood creation at scale. Precursor: SOF builds on the Skill Impact Bond (SIB) launched in 2021, which demonstrated the success of outcomes-based financing by deploying ~Rs.130 crore to train 34,000+ youth across 21 states (74% women) and achieving 92% certification, 76% job placement, and 62% retention rates exceeding national benchmarks. About National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC): NSDC is a not-for-profit public limited company set up in 2008 as a Public Private Partnership (PPP), with 49% stake held by the Government of India (GoI) through the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) and 51% by the private sector. Chief Executive Officer (CEO) – Arunkumar Pillai Headquarters – New Delhi, Delhi Established – 2008 NITI Aayog Launches Report on ‘Women’s Evolving Credit Market’; Women Hold Rs. 76 Lakh Crore Credit Portfolio In April 2026, Nidhi Chhibber, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog, released the second edition of its report titled “From Borrowers to Builders: Women and India’s Evolving Credit Market” in New Delhi, Delhi. • The report highlights that women hold a credit portfolio of Rs.76 lakh crore, accounting for 26% of total system credit with a 4.8-fold rise since 2017. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Report “From Borrowers to Builders: Women and India’s Evolving Credit Market” released ✓ By whom? Nidhi Chhibber, CEO, NITI Aayog ✓ Collaboration: WEP, TransUnion CIBIL, MicroSave Consulting ✓ Women’s Credit Portfolio: Rs.76 lakh crore (26% of total system credit) ✓ Credit Penetration: Increased to 36% in 2025 ✓ Credit-Active Women Borrowers: Approximately 16 crore ✓ CAGR (2017-2025): 9% for credit-active women borrowers ✓ Emerging growth states: Bihar and UP. Key Highlights: Dignitaries: The event was attended by dignitaries including Anna Roy (Programme Director, NITI Aayog & Mission Director, WEP); Neelam Patel, Rajib Kumar Sen, Ishtiyaque Ahmed, and Sonia Pant (Programme Directors, NITI Aayog); Swapnalee Bhattacharya (Deputy Director General (DDG), NITI Aayog); Mercy Epao (Joint Secretary, Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MoMSME)); Bhavesh Jain (Managing Director (MD) & CEO, TransUnion CIBIL); and Akhand Tiwari (Senior Partner, MicroSave Consulting (MSC)). Collaboration: The report, prepared under the aegis of the Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP), was developed by TransUnion CIBIL in collaboration with MicroSave Consulting (MSC). Objective: Initiated by the WEP in 2025 under the Financing Women Collaborative (FWC), the report addresses gaps in sex-disaggregated data on women’s access to formal credit, including trends, borrower behaviour, and credit progression.

# Page 30^page=30
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 30 Daily Content PDF Methodology: The findings are based on longitudinal credit bureau data of approximately 16 crore credit- active women, supplemented by primary research involving 161 rural women nano-entrepreneurs, offering both quantitative and behavioural insights. This edition also incorporates microfinance data, providing a more comprehensive assessment of women’s access to and progression within the credit ecosystem. Key Findings: Penetration: Credit penetration among women increased from 19% in 2017 to 36% in 2025 with around 16 crore credit-active borrowers growing at a 9% Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR). Potential: Nearly 45 crore credit-eligible women exist in India, with about two-thirds still unserved, indicating vast expansion scope. Shift: Women are moving from entry-level loans to retail and business lending, with 19% of Microfinance Institution (MFI) borrowers transitioning to mainstream credit. Commercial: Credit to women entrepreneurs grew at a 31% CAGR during 2022–2025, surpassing overall commercial credit growth of 17%, alongside a 7.5 times rise in women entrepreneurs’ portfolios Products: Personal and gold loans dominate, while housing loans are increasing, reflecting rising asset ownership. Geography: Credit access is expanding beyond southern and western regions to northern states like Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (UP). Digital: Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) across identity, payments, underwriting, and servicing has reduced barriers and enabled formal credit inclusion. Recommendations: Key suggestions include gender-bias audits, gender-intelligent financial products, youth-focused credit pathways, and integration of credit, savings, and digital financial literacy. About National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog: Chief Executive Officer (CEO) – Nidhi Chhibber Headquarters – New Delhi, Delhi Established – 2015 India Withdraws Proposal To Host COP 33 Climate Summit 2028 In April 2026, India officially withdrew its proposal to host COP33 under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in 2028, leaving South Korea as the sole bidder. • Rajat Agarwal, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change (MoEFCC) informed the chair of United Nation (UN) Asia-Pacific Group (currently Pakistan), within the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (which conducts the climate conference) via letter, citing a ‘review of its commitments’. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Withdrawal of proposal to host COP33 in 2028 ✓ Who? India ✓ Announced by: Rajat Agarwal, Joint Secretary, MoEFCC ✓ Reason: Review of its commitments ✓ Next Bidder: South Korea. Key Details: India’s Proposal: Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi had conveyed India’s proposal to host COP33 during his special address at the inauguration of the High-Level Segment (HLS) of COP28 in December 2023 in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Previous COP Hosting: India previously hosted only COP8 in 2002 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, Delhi. COP: It is the highest decision-making body under the UNFCCC, where Parties meet annually to assess progress on climate goals, negotiate commitments, and mobilise climate finance and action.

# Page 31^page=31
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 31 Daily Content PDF Union MoS Dr. Jitendra Singh Announces Seismological Observatory and Doppler Radar In April 2026, Union Minister of State (MoS) (Independent Charge, IC) Dr. Jitendra Singh, Ministry of Science & Technology (MoS&T) and Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) announced the establishment of a Seismological Observatory in Kishtwar and a Doppler Weather Radar (DWR) in Doda in Jammu and Kashmir(J&K). • He made the announcement while chairing a meeting of the District Development Coordination and Monitoring Committee (DISHA) at the DC Office Complex in Doda. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Announcement of a Seismological Observatory, DWR ✓ Who? Union MoS (IC) Dr. Jitendra Singh, Minister, MoS&T ✓ Occasion: During DISHA meeting ✓ Where? J&K ✓ Key Installations: ✓ Seismological Observatory – Kishtwar ✓ Doppler Weather Radar – Doda ✓ Purpose: To enhance earthquake monitoring, improve weather forecasting, and strengthen early warning systems. Significance of Initiative: Doppler Weather Radar (DWR): The proposed DWR will facilitate precise, real-time monitoring of weather conditions, significantly enhancing early warning systems and strengthening disaster management capabilities in the district under the Mission Mausam initiative. Seismological Observatory: The establishment of a permanent seismological observatory will augment India’s national seismic monitoring network, improve earthquake detection and analysis, and reinforce disaster preparedness and risk mitigation in the region. Automated Weather Stations (AWS): He also announced that site selection has been completed for installing AWS in the remote areas of Paddar and Machail to enhance weather forecasting and strengthen disaster management efforts. Significance: These initiatives support the expansion of India’s meteorological and seismic observation networks, particularly in vulnerable mountainous regions. ALEMAI Launches ‘Aluminium Bharat’ Initiative to Boost Domestic Manufacturing and Global Competitiveness In April 2026, the Aluminium Extrusion Manufacturers Association of India (ALEMAI) has launched the ‘Aluminium Bharat’ initiative to enhance domestic manufacturing capabilities, promote sustainable industrial growth, and position India as a global leader in aluminium production and exports. • The initiative was unveiled by Union Minister of State (MoS) Jitin Prasada, Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I) in New Delhi, Delhi. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of ‘Aluminium Bharat’ ✓ Launched by: Union Mos Jitin Prasada, MoC&I ✓ Organised By: Aluminium Extrusion Manufacturers Association of India ✓ Objective: Boost domestic aluminium manufacturing and enhance global competitiveness ✓ Key Event: Aluminium Bharat 2026, scheduled in September 2026 ✓ Alignment: India’s USD 5 trillion economy; Viksit Bharat 2047.
